ledger.summary: A man seeks Ralph: Morfinn the Minstrel, short, fat, pale with pink cheeks, long curling yellow hair, a thin red beard and blue eyes, unlike the local folk, in orange-tawny and silver. He claims to know Well-lore, the way through Utterness, and a sage near Utterness who can set seekers on the road, and says he has news of the damsel for Ralph's ear alone. He shows a three-month-old safe-conduct from Gandolf, Lord of Utterbol, sealed with the Bear upon the Castle Wall, without which the road is deadly. Ralph chooses to go with him alone rather than with an armed escort or Bull. Clement distrusts Morfinn; Ralph is drawn on by thoughts of the damsel.
ledger.geography_notes: Between Goldburg and Utterbol's lands lies a debatable land; no small unknown band can cross it or Utterbol's lands. They will leave by Goldburg's east gate.
